title: Back to SQLite
messages: hearth keeps dying. the pi is swaping like crazy and influx is the reason, its using 1.2 gb of the 4
InfluxDB plus Grafana in containers on a 4 GB Pi 4 is tight. Options: tune Influx's cache and shard settings, move Grafana off the Pi, or go back to SQLite, which uses almost nothing.
grafana was nice but its not worth a pi that falls over. going back to sqlite. i was right the first time, one file, no server to babysit. flip the collector back
Switched collector.py back to SQLite using the existing file, and backfilled the 16 days of readings that Influx holds. Removed influxdb and grafana from docker-compose.
and the export script needs to read from sqlite now
Updated scripts/export_week.py to query SQLite. It is still a Python script and still runs from cron on Sundays.
good. for charts ill just use the csv in a spreadsheet, fine
That works. If you want a quick chart without a server later, a static HTML page generated by the same script is an option.
memory use down to 300mb total. relief

title: Rust course, lesson 5
messages: did lesson 5 finally. took a week off. honestly im not sure this course is worth my evenings. hearthd already works and its my only rust service
That is a fair thing to ask. A course is worth the time if it gets you to something you will use. Is there a second service you would want to write in Rust?
not really, not right now. i still like rust for services, i just have no time. the course has 3 more lessons and idk if ill finish
You could keep the part that pays off for you, which is understanding ownership well enough to maintain hearthd, and treat the rest as optional.
hm. alex m will be annoyed, hes been so keen. ill decide after lesson 6
Deciding after one more lesson is a reasonable way to handle it.
also is it just me or does the course get less fun every week
It is common. The first lessons give quick wins, and the later ones ask for more patience.
yeah. ok bed, dog needs his last walk

title: Moved to Bath
messages: im in!! moved to bath yesterday. biscuit claimed the sofa within 10 mins
Congratulations on the move. A sofa claimed in ten minutes is a good sign that he is settling in. How was the first night?
he slept through. so im not in clifton any more, i live in bath now. the walk to the office is gone, its the train from tuesday
That is a big change of routine. Forty minutes on the train gives you time to read or switch off, depending on the day.
ill use it for the rust course notes, if i keep going with that lol
Notes are a good fit for a train: no setup, and you can stop at any station.
the garden is tiny but biscuit loves it. the flat is much warmer than the old one
Good. Is there anything left to sort out from the move?
hearth will need redoing for the new boiler though. later.
Later is fine. When you do, note where the new boiler's controls are before you plan the relay.

title: Queue outcome and the status page
messages: update on the outbox queue. its been running 2 weeks, about 40k events a day, no trouble. only complaint is notifications arriving up to 5 seconds late, support noticed
That matches the 5 second poll interval. Dropping it to 1 second is cheap with SKIP LOCKED and an index on the status column. Want me to change it?
yes, 1 second. lesson learned: pick the poll interval from what support needs, not from whats easy. and glad we didnt do rabbit
Changed to 1 second, and made the interval a config value.
now the status page. write the availability line for next week for the team page. im in mon, tue, wed and fri
Which day or days are you out next week, and do you want a reason on the line?
Here is the line: 'Noor: in Mon-Wed and Fri; out Thursday afternoon.'
good. btw i still havent decided on the platform team thing. imogen mentioned a platform opening in the spring. ill think
A spring opening gives you a few weeks. It may help to write down what you would miss about Atlas and what you would gain on the platform team.

title: Running again
messages: ok bath has hills and flat river paths. i think i want to start running again. maybe a 5k this time, in may. the dog is settled so evenings are free again
A 5k in May gives you about fourteen weeks, which is plenty for a gentle build-up. Do you want a plan?
yes. not the 10k, the 10k is dead. just a 5k. i got the waterproof trail shoes in the end so no excuses
A fourteen-week plan: three runs a week, starting with run-walk intervals of 20 minutes, and moving to continuous running by week 6.
mon wed sat again. and biscuit can come on the easy ones
Greyhounds are sprinters rather than distance runners, so keep his runs short and easy, and let him decide when he has had enough.
ha ok. 5k in may then. starting monday
Monday it is. Week 1: three runs of 20 minutes, one minute running and one minute walking.

messages: alex p approved the import check pr. he said hes still going to push graphql later but its fine for now
Good. The import-boundary check is merged to main.
ok the runbook. you offered a draft weeks ago, lets do it. ingest check, replaying events from the outbox, who to call

Drafted RUNBOOK.md. 1. Is ingest running: the health endpoint and the events-per-minute graph. 2. Replaying events from the outbox. 3. If the outbox backs up. 4. Who to call: Imogen first, then Alex Pryce.
put me as the first call, not imogen. and alex p second
Updated: Noor, then Alex Pryce, then Imogen.
good. ill add the rollback steps for migrations too, thats what got us
A migration rollback section is a good addition. Start with the order: roll back the app first, then the schema.

title: Alex's notes and threads versus async
messages: alex m sent his course notes, theyre really good. he also thinks i should finish the course, says the last 3 lessons are the best ones
Good notes can make the later lessons much easier. Are you leaning towards finishing?
i tried what you said last time and measured hearthd, threads vs async. the thread version uses 2mb more memory, nothing else visible. so im keeping threads for hearthd
A 2 MB difference on a Pi is small, and you have a measurement to go with the choice. That is a solid reason to keep the simpler design.
the course people will say async anyway lol. async is for if i ever write something that takes lots of connections
That is a sensible rule of thumb: threads for small fixed workloads, async when the number of connections can grow.
still undecided on finishing. lesson 6 is on tuesday
Then Tuesday is when you decide. You do not need to settle it tonight.

title: Booking the trek
messages: update on the morocco trip: my sister said yes to biscuit sitting. booking flights tonight, 17 to 22 april
That is the biggest blocker gone. Check the flight times, because an early departure from Bristol makes the first day much easier.
found them, bristol to marrakech 175 pounds return with a bag
That is a good price. Book the first night in Imlil as well, since that is the bed most likely to fill up.
jo is going to book the guide. 5 days, shared, about 150 each
Then you have about 375 pounds left for guesthouses, food and transfers, which is enough if you stay in local guesthouses.
